title: Nobody, No-one and Nothing
summary: Say that no person or thing is involved using nobody, no-one and nothing. Use anybody, anyone or anything after negative verbs without creating a double negative.
learningObjectives: Choose nobody or no-one for people, and nothing for things.
Rewrite negative statements using not anybody, not anyone or not anything without changing meaning.
Use nobody, no-one and nothing as subjects and short answers.
Avoid double negatives when describing the absence of people or things.

explanation.heading: Negative forms for people
explanation.body: Anybody and anyone refer to people. After a negative verb, not anybody or not anyone means zero people. Nobody and no-one carry this negative meaning by themselves and normally take a positive verb. Nobody and no-one mean the same thing.
explanation.example: The bakery was closed, so I did not see anyone there.

explanation.heading: Negative forms for things
explanation.body: Anything refers to an unspecified thing. Not anything means zero things. Nothing gives that negative meaning without a negative verb. It can describe objects, activities, information or events, depending on context.
explanation.example: I opened the envelope, but there was nothing inside.

explanation.heading: Use negative words as subjects
explanation.body: Nobody, no-one and nothing can begin a sentence and act as its subject. In the present simple they normally take a singular verb such as knows, wants or happens. Do not add a second negative to a sentence that already has nobody or nothing.
explanation.example: Nobody knows the code for the old cupboard.

explanation.heading: Give short answers to who and what
explanation.body: In a short answer, nobody or no-one answers who, while nothing answers what. The form is chosen by whether the question is about a person or a thing, not by the verb tense in the question.

explanation.heading: Avoid double negatives in standard English
explanation.body: To say zero people or things, use either a negative verb plus anybody, anyone or anything, or a positive verb plus nobody, no-one or nothing. Mixing did not with nobody or nothing can change the meaning or produce a nonstandard negative.
explanation.example: The team did not receive anything by post.

comparisons.title: Two ways to say zero people

left.label: Negative verb + anyone
left.example: I did not meet anyone at the station.
left.note: Did not carries the negative meaning.

right.label: Positive verb + no-one
right.example: I met no-one at the station.
right.note: No-one carries the negative meaning without not.

examples.sentence: There was nobody behind the counter when I entered.
examples.note: Nobody refers to people; there was is not negative.

examples.sentence: I did not hear anything during the night.
examples.note: Anything follows a negative verb and refers to sounds or events.

examples.sentence: Nothing happened after the lights went out.
examples.note: Nothing is the subject and takes a positive singular verb.
No-one can be a short answer to who.

examples.sentence: We have nothing to prepare for tomorrow.
examples.note: Nothing is followed by an infinitive phrase explaining what is absent.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I didn't see nobody at the gate.
commonMistakes.correct: I didn't see anybody at the gate.
commonMistakes.why: Use anybody after a negative verb in standard English.

commonMistakes.incorrect: There was not nothing in the cupboard.
commonMistakes.correct: There was nothing in the cupboard.
commonMistakes.why: Nothing already expresses the negative meaning; the verb should stay positive.
A who question asks about a person, so answer with nobody or no-one.
Nobody is grammatically singular and takes knows in the present simple.

studyTips: Ask whether the missing information is a person or a thing before choosing a negative pronoun.
To check a negative sentence, look for not: after it, use anybody, anyone or anything for the zero meaning.
Make two versions of short examples: “I saw nobody” and “I did not see anyone”.

exercises.prompt: The building was closed and the staff had gone home. There was ___ inside.
exercises.feedback: Nobody means no person remained; the positive verb was is correct.

exercises.prompt: The food cupboard is empty. There is ___ to eat.
exercises.feedback: Nothing refers to the absence of food, which is a thing rather than a person.

exercises.prompt: My phone was switched off, so I did not hear ___.
exercises.feedback: Did not is negative, so use anything rather than nothing.

exercises.prompt: Who answered the door when you arrived? ___ .
exercises.feedback: Who asks about a person; nobody is the appropriate short answer.

exercises.prompt: Choose anybody or nobody: The classroom is empty. There is ___ here.
exercises.feedback: Nobody works with the positive verb is to mean there are no people.

exercises.prompt: Choose anything or nothing: I cannot find ___ in this drawer.
exercises.feedback: Cannot is negative, so use anything.

exercises.prompt: Choose anyone or no-one: ___ knows the secret. I have not told a single person.
exercises.feedback: No-one is the negative subject, so the positive verb knows is correct.

exercises.prompt: Choose anything or nothing: We searched the suitcase, but we found ___.
exercises.feedback: Nothing carries the zero-quantity meaning with the positive verb found.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence for the meaning “not one person called”: Nobody did not call me this morning.
exercises.feedback: Nobody already expresses no person, so remove did not and use the past simple called.

exercises.prompt: Keep the negative verb and correct the sentence: I do not need nothing from the shop.
acceptedAnswers: I do not need anything from the shop.
I don't need anything from the shop.
exercises.feedback: With do not, anything expresses zero things without a second negative.

exercises.prompt: Replace nobody with anybody and correct the sentence: There is not nobody at the desk.
acceptedAnswers: There is not anybody at the desk.
There isn't anybody at the desk.
exercises.feedback: Not anybody is the negative-verb structure; nobody would add another negative.

exercises.prompt: Replace only the first word to correct the description of an empty box: Anything is inside the box.
exercises.feedback: Nothing is the negative subject that means the box contains no objects.

speakingExercises.prompt: You are saying that zero people came to the picnic. Say a complete sentence beginning “Nobody” and ending “to the picnic”.
speakingExercises.feedback: Nobody is the subject; the past tense came expresses the event without an additional negative.

speakingExercises.prompt: You are alone in a room. Say a complete sentence using “There is not” and “anyone”.
acceptedAnswers: There is not anyone in the room.
There isn't anyone in the room.
There's not anyone in the room.
speakingExercises.feedback: A negative verb plus anyone states that no person is in the room.

speakingExercises.prompt: You have zero information to report. Say a complete sentence beginning “I have” and using nothing.
speakingExercises.feedback: Nothing stands for the information that is absent, and have is positive.

speakingExercises.prompt: Not one person wants a late meeting. Say one sentence beginning 'Nobody' and using the correct present-simple form of 'want' with 'a late meeting'.
speakingExercises.feedback: Nobody is a singular subject, so want becomes wants in the present simple.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change 'We heard nothing in the hallway' into one complete sentence using 'did not' or 'didn't' and 'anything'. Keep the subject and place.
acceptedAnswers: We did not hear anything in the hallway.
We didn't hear anything in the hallway.
speakingExercises.feedback: Did not hear anything and heard nothing express the same absence of sounds.

speakingExercises.prompt: Your friend asks, 'Who collected the lost umbrella?' You know that no person collected it. Give a one-word short answer using 'nobody'.
speakingExercises.feedback: Nobody and no-one are natural short answers to who; nothing would refer to a thing.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct 'Nobody don't live here' to say that no people live here. Begin with 'Nobody' and use the correct present-simple form of 'live'.
speakingExercises.feedback: Nobody already carries negative meaning and takes the singular positive verb lives.

speakingExercises.prompt: You searched a cupboard and found zero objects. There was also no person in the room. Say two short sentences: start with 'I found' and then 'There was'; use 'nothing' and 'no one'.
acceptedAnswers: I found nothing. There was no one in the room.
speakingExercises.feedback: Nothing refers to objects, and no-one refers to people; neither needs a negative verb.

listeningExercises.audioText: Nobody recognised the new neighbour at the party.
listeningExercises.prompt: What does the speaker say about the new neighbour?
choices: Not one person recognised the neighbour.
The neighbour did not attend the party.
listeningExercises.feedback: Nobody means zero people recognised the neighbour.

listeningExercises.audioText: I did not find anything under the sofa.
listeningExercises.prompt: What did the speaker find under the sofa?
listeningExercises.feedback: Did not find anything means that no object was found.

listeningExercises.audioText: Nobody answered when I knocked on the door.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the first word you hear: the negative word that refers to people.
listeningExercises.feedback: Nobody means not one person answered the door.

listeningExercises.audioText: Nothing was missing from my bag after the bus ride.
choices: A friend had taken the bag.
All their belongings were still there.
listeningExercises.feedback: Nothing was missing means that not one item had disappeared.

listeningExercises.audioText: The bus stopped at the school, but nobody got on.
listeningExercises.feedback: Nobody got on means that zero people boarded at the stop.

listeningExercises.audioText: I didn't receive anything by email, but a letter arrived this morning.
choices: A physical letter rather than an email.
Both an email and a letter.
listeningExercises.feedback: Didn't receive anything by email rules out an email, but the speaker did receive a letter.

listeningExercises.audioText: Nobody knows why the lights went off last night.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the first word of the sentence, showing how many people know the reason.
listeningExercises.feedback: Nobody means not one person, and it takes the singular verb knows.

listeningExercises.audioText: The children searched the garden, but they didn't find anything.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the final word you hear, which refers to an unspecified thing.
listeningExercises.feedback: Anything follows the negative verb didn't find to mean that no object was found.
